title: The Incident
briefing: A severe AI-enabled attack has hit the UK. Services are disrupted, the cause is public, and ministers want a response today. You have minutes, not months, and the advice in the room is not agreed.

forecast.question: Chance of a further disruptive AI-enabled attack on the UK before the end of 2032.

shah.stance: One incident tells us little about the base rate. Respond to the damage; do not legislate from the wreckage.

memory.line: James will say the 2027 pact caused this. From one incident, nobody in this room can know whether evaluation at the border would have stopped it.

harcourt.stance: This is the warning. Mandate agent security standards now, while Parliament will pass them.

memory.line: In 2027 I asked for evaluation before market access. We chose a reporting pact.
In 2027 we welcomed the open-weight release. I said then that every safeguard on it was optional.

chen.stance: Liability written in a week will be litigated for a decade, and a provider may simply leave. Use the law we have.

okafor.stance: People lost power and water. They need to see that someone is accountable when a deployment is negligent.

choices.text: Respond under existing law with national cyber support.
choices.headline: Government responds to the attack under existing law, with national cyber support for operators.
Emergency agent security standards take effect for every system offered in the UK.
Providers become liable for negligent deployment of AI agents in the UK.
The government's own incident-response model is deployed to contain the attack; recovery is measured in hours.

evidencePanel.known: The UK's official assessment is that AI will raise the frequency and intensity of intrusions. Research on focusing events shows that regulation tends to follow disasters rather than precede them.
evidencePanel.unknown: Whether this attack marks a change in the base rate or one draw from the rate you already faced.
evidencePanel.whyItMatters: Restriction is cheapest after the harm and most expensive when it would have prevented it.

sources.label: NCSC, Impact of AI on cyber threat from now to 2027
Birkland, Focusing Events, Mobilization, and Agenda Setting (1998)
